meta.title: Scholarship Opportunity Dashboard
meta.disclaimer: This is a curated starter database, not a live feed. Scholarship amounts, deadlines, and rules typically change every year — always confirm current details on the official Website URL before applying. Use the 'Last Verified' date on each record as a guide to how fresh the entry is.

A.label: Candidate A — Brown University, Class of 2030
A.description: First-year student entering Brown University in Fall 2026. U.S. citizen, first time living/resident in the U.S. Admitted as Undeclared, intending Cognitive Neuroscience. Nigerian origin (eligible for African-descent minority scholarships).

B.label: Candidate B — UK-based, 11th Grade (Year 12)
B.description: Dual American/British citizen residing in the UK, entering 11th grade (Year 12). Interested in Business, Psychology, and Finance. Nigerian origin (eligible for African-descent minority scholarships). Not yet a graduating senior — many awards below apply once she reaches 12th grade, flagged in 'Candidate B Fit'.

scholarships.name: Coca-Cola Scholars Program
scholarships.amount_display: $20,000 (one-time, achievement-based)
scholarships.deadline: Opens Aug 3, 2026 — closes Sept 30, 2026 (for HS seniors graduating 2026-27)
eligible_stage: High school senior (apply fall of 12th grade)
scholarships.residency_notes: No requirement to live in the U.S.; open to citizens abroad. Must enroll full-time at an accredited U.S. college the following fall.
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable — restricted to graduating high school seniors, not already-enrolled college students.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Future opportunity — apply fall of 12th grade (~2027).
scholarships.notes: One of the largest no-restriction merit scholarships in the U.S.; 150 scholars selected annually.

scholarships.name: Jack Kent Cooke College Scholarship
scholarships.amount_display: Last-dollar award, up to $55,000/year (2026 cycle), renewable up to 4 years
eligible_stage: High school senior with financial need (top academic performers)
scholarships.residency_notes: Must plan to enroll full-time at an accredited 4-year U.S. institution.
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable — for incoming (not currently-enrolled) high school seniors.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Future opportunity — apply fall of 12th grade. Strong fit given need-based + high-achievement design.
scholarships.notes: Highly competitive; requires substantial financial need documentation.

scholarships.name: Horatio Alger National & State Scholarships
scholarships.amount_display: State awards up to $10,000; National awards $25,000
eligible_stage: High school senior with demonstrated financial hardship
scholarships.residency_notes: Must attend U.S. high school and enroll full-time at a U.S. institution.
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable — for incoming high school seniors, not enrolled college students.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Future opportunity — apply senior year if attending a U.S.-based high school for the application; UK-based schooling may complicate the 'U.S. high school' requirement, verify with the Association.
scholarships.notes: Emphasizes overcoming adversity; requires a critical financial-need essay.

scholarships.name: Ron Brown Scholar Program
scholarships.amount_display: $40,000 total ($10,000/year x 4 years)
eligible_stage: High school senior
scholarships.residency_notes: Open to African American / Black seniors nationwide.
scholarships.minority_group: African American / Black (Nigerian-heritage/African-descent students commonly qualify)
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable — for incoming high school seniors, not enrolled college students.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Future opportunity — apply fall of 12th grade. Strong fit as a Black/African-descent student interested in business.
scholarships.notes: Emphasizes public service, entrepreneurship, and community engagement — pairs well with Candidate B's business interest.

scholarships.name: The Gates Scholarship
scholarships.provider: Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation / Scholarship America
scholarships.amount_display: Last-dollar, covers full unmet need (varies; commonly $5,000-$80,000+ over 4 years)
eligible_stage: High school senior, Pell-eligible / low-income
scholarships.residency_notes: Minimum 3.3 GPA; must be Pell-Grant eligible.
scholarships.minority_group: African American, American Indian/Alaska Native, Asian & Pacific Islander American, or Hispanic American
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable — for incoming high school seniors, not enrolled college students.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Future opportunity — apply fall of 12th grade if income-eligible.
scholarships.notes: One of the largest last-dollar minority scholarships; highly selective.

scholarships.name: QuestBridge National College Match
scholarships.amount_display: Full four-year scholarship (tuition, room & board) at partner colleges
eligible_stage: High school senior, low-income/high-achieving
citizenship: Any (including international, with some partner-school restrictions)
scholarships.residency_notes: Open to U.S. and international applicants; check each partner college's international-aid policy.
scholarships.school_specific: Brown University is a QuestBridge partner college
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable this cycle — Match happens before matriculation; A has already been admitted/committed to Brown.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Future opportunity — apply fall of 12th grade; Brown is a Match college, directly relevant if she later targets Brown.
scholarships.notes: Brown University participates as a College Match Partner — worth flagging to younger siblings/relatives applying in future cycles.

scholarships.name: Elks National Foundation Most Valuable Student (MVS) Scholarship
scholarships.amount_display: $4,000-$30,000 total over 4 years (500 awards; top 20 scholars receive $30,000)
eligible_stage: High school senior
scholarships.residency_notes: Applicant or parent typically must reside in an area with an active Elks Lodge (most U.S. ZIP codes qualify).
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable — for incoming high school seniors.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Future opportunity, and only if a parent/guardian has U.S. residency tied to an Elks Lodge jurisdiction — verify eligibility given UK residence.
scholarships.notes: Only the top-tier awards ($30,000, plus 480 runner-ups at $4,000) are shown; lower per-year tiers can fall below $5,000/year.

scholarships.name: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
scholarships.deadline: 2027 cycle opens Fall 2026 (2026 cycle closed Feb 18, 2026)
eligible_stage: Age 18 or under, any schooling status, with a completed significant original project
citizenship: incl. those living abroad on U.S. military status
scholarships.residency_notes: Open to applicants living outside the U.S. if citizenship criteria are met — verify current-year residency rules.
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable — requires an unsubmitted, original project and typically targets pre-college applicants.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Possible fit if she completes an independent research project in business, psychology, or finance/economics before turning 18.
scholarships.notes: Rewards original research/creative projects, not just academic record — could pair with a neuroscience research project for a younger sibling in the future.

scholarships.name: Burger King McLamore Scholars Program
scholarships.amount_display: $1,000-$60,000 (most awards $1,000-$5,000; three top awards of $60,000)
eligible_stage: High school senior
scholarships.residency_notes: Minimum 2.5 GPA, community service focus.
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable — for incoming high school seniors.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Future opportunity — apply fall of 12th grade. Only the top 3 awards ($60,000) clear the $5,000 floor; most awards are smaller.
scholarships.notes: Community-service oriented; verify current-year tier structure since most awards are below $5,000.

scholarships.name: AXA Achievement Scholarship (Ambition Award)
scholarships.amount_display: $2,500-$25,000 (only $5,000+ tiers qualify for the 'no maximum, $5k floor' filter)
eligible_stage: High school senior
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable — for incoming high school seniors.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Future opportunity — apply fall of 12th grade.
scholarships.notes: Rewards ambition/self-drive and risk management-related essay prompts — could resonate with a finance-interested applicant.

scholarships.name: Dell Scholars Program
scholarships.amount_display: $20,000 over 4 years + laptop + wraparound support
eligible_stage: High school senior, Pell-eligible, in an approved college-readiness program
scholarships.residency_notes: Requires participation in an approved college-access/readiness program — verify UK-based equivalents are not accepted.
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable — for incoming high school seniors.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Likely not applicable — requires enrollment in a specific U.S. college-readiness program list; unlikely available in the UK. Verify directly.
scholarships.notes: Strong fit for low-income first-generation students; program-participation requirement is the key barrier.

scholarships.name: Bank of America Student Leaders Program
scholarships.amount_display: $5,000 stipend + paid 6-8 week nonprofit internship + Washington, D.C. Leadership Summit
eligible_stage: Current high school junior or senior (11th or 12th grade)
citizenship: U.S. residency/eligibility to work required for the local internship placement — verify for UK-based applicants
scholarships.residency_notes: Program is run through local U.S. markets; students typically need to be near a participating market. Confirm whether UK-based/international applicants can participate.
scholarships.nomination_notes: Requires a recommendation from a teacher, counselor, or community leader (not a formal school nomination).
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable — restricted to current high school juniors/seniors.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Directly eligible now as an 11th grader — strong fit for her business/finance interest, though the U.S.-market internship logistics need confirming given UK residence.
scholarships.notes: One of the few nationally-known programs open to juniors, not just seniors.

scholarships.name: DECA Inc. Scholarships — Anderson Advisors Award
scholarships.amount_display: $5,000 (4 awards)
eligible_stage: High school junior, senior, or current college student
citizenship: Open to DECA members; check nationality requirements on current guidelines
scholarships.residency_notes: Requires active DECA membership; DECA has limited international chapters — verify a UK-based chapter or affiliate option.
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable — business/finance focus does not match Cognitive Neuroscience, and program targets DECA members.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Directly eligible now as an 11th grader interested in finance, if she can join a DECA chapter (in-person or DECA Direct virtual membership) — verify international membership options.
scholarships.notes: DECA also offers smaller $2,000 general awards (below the $5,000 floor, not listed here).

scholarships.name: Goldwater Scholarship
eligible_stage: College sophomore or junior (not freshman) intending a research PhD in natural sciences, math, engineering, or behavioral/cognitive neuroscience
scholarships.nomination_notes: Requires official institutional nomination — but from the COLLEGE (Brown's Goldwater faculty representative), not the high school. Brown nominates a limited number of students annually.
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Future opportunity — not eligible as a first-year; becomes eligible in sophomore/junior year. Excellent long-term match for her Cognitive Neuroscience research trajectory at Brown. She should connect with Brown's Fellowships Office early.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Not applicable — for currently-enrolled U.S. college sophomores/juniors.
scholarships.notes: The premier U.S. undergraduate award for future research scientists; flagged here for A's freshman-year planning even though not currently actionable.

scholarships.name: SMART Scholarship (Science, Mathematics & Research for Transformation)
scholarships.amount_display: Full tuition/fees + $28,000-$46,000 annual stipend + guaranteed DoD employment
eligible_stage: Rising sophomore, junior, senior, or graduate student in an eligible STEM major, incl. Cognitive Science
scholarships.residency_notes: Requires ability to obtain a security clearance and accept post-graduate DoD employment (service commitment).
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Future opportunity — typically requires declared major and rising-sophomore standing; worth tracking once she declares Cognitive Neuroscience. Involves a post-grad DoD work commitment, an important trade-off to weigh.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Not applicable — U.S. college STEM majors only.
scholarships.notes: Very large award, but comes with a mandatory multi-year DoD service obligation after graduation.

scholarships.name: Brown University Need-Based Financial Aid (Institutional Grant)
scholarships.provider: Brown University Office of Financial Aid
scholarships.amount_display: Meets 100% of demonstrated financial need (no-loan policy); total cost of attendance is ~$92,400 (billed) to ~$102,000 (full COA) for 2025-26, and aid varies by family finances
scholarships.deadline: CSS Profile/FAFSA typically due with admission application; incoming students should confirm with Financial Aid office
eligible_stage: All enrolled undergraduates, including first-years
citizenship: international (Brown is need-blind/need-aware by citizenship category — verify current policy)
scholarships.residency_notes: Brown does not offer merit scholarships — all institutional aid is need-based.
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Directly applicable now — Brown's primary funding source; important to note it is need-based, not merit-based, and requires the family's financial documentation.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Not applicable — she is not enrolled at Brown.
scholarships.notes: Brown has no institutional merit scholarships; all 'Brown-specific' funding beyond this is via named endowed funds administered case-by-case through the Financial Aid office.

scholarships.name: Cameron Impact Scholarship
scholarships.amount_display: Full 4-year tuition, fees, and books (est. $20,000-$80,000+ total, school-dependent)
scholarships.deadline: Two windows historically — an early ~May deadline and a regular ~September deadline (Class-year specific), or when the ~3,000-application cap is hit, whichever comes first
eligible_stage: High school senior, minimum 3.7 unweighted GPA
scholarships.residency_notes: Must plan to enroll full-time at an accredited 4-year U.S. institution.
scholarships.nomination_notes: REQUIRES official nomination by the student's high school (counselor or school official submits the nomination before the student can apply).
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable — for incoming high school seniors, not already-enrolled students.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Future opportunity — she should tell her high school counselor now (start of 11th grade) that she wants to be nominated when senior applications open, since the school controls the nomination step.
scholarships.notes: One of the most generous full-tuition awards; the school-nomination requirement is the single biggest logistical hurdle — start the conversation with the counselor early.

scholarships.name: Jefferson Scholars Program (University of Virginia)
scholarships.amount_display: Full cost of attendance at UVA (4 years)
eligible_stage: High school senior
citizenship: U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident (international track available separately)
scholarships.residency_notes: School-specific to the University of Virginia only.
scholarships.nomination_notes: REQUIRES high school counselor nomination — one of the clearest national examples of a nomination-gated award.
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable — tied to UVA, not Brown, and restricted to incoming seniors.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Only relevant if she later adds UVA to her college list; included here as a landscape example of a nomination-required program, since the family asked to see these clearly.
scholarships.notes: Included primarily to illustrate the 'school must nominate' category requested — swap for a Brown-track equivalent if she considers UVA.

scholarships.name: UNCF Scholarship Portal (Corporate & General Scholars Programs)
scholarships.amount_display: Varies by specific award; several corporate-sponsored awards $5,000-$27,500
scholarships.deadline: Varies by individual award — portal opens applications ~spring/summer annually
eligible_stage: High school senior or current undergraduate, depending on specific award
citizenship: U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident (most awards)
scholarships.residency_notes: Many (not all) UNCF awards restrict eligible schools to HBCUs or UNCF member institutions — Brown does NOT qualify for those; a subset of awards are open to any accredited 4-year U.S. institution. Check each award individually.
scholarships.minority_group: Black / African American / African descent (Nigerian-heritage students qualify)
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Partial — only the subset of UNCF awards NOT restricted to HBCU/member schools would apply to a Brown student; filter carefully on the portal by 'any accredited institution.'
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Future opportunity — same caveat applies once she is a college applicant/enrollee.
scholarships.notes: UNCF is the largest minority scholarship clearinghouse in the U.S.; treat this row as a portal entry point rather than a single award.

scholarships.name: National Association of Black Accountants (NABA) National Scholarship
scholarships.amount_display: $1,000-$10,000 (average ~150 awards/year)
eligible_stage: Currently-enrolled 2-year or 4-year college student (NOT open to high schoolers)
citizenship: Open to Black/African-descent students; U.S. enrollment required
scholarships.minority_group: Black / African American / African descent (Nigerian-heritage students qualify)
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable — accounting/finance focus doesn't match Cognitive Neuroscience.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Future opportunity — once enrolled in a U.S. college studying finance/business; NABA also runs a pre-college 'Accounting & Finance Pipeline' program worth exploring now (not a scholarship, but a pipeline into one).
scholarships.notes: Strong long-term option once B is in college; not currently actionable for either candidate.

scholarships.name: IABA Foundation Scholarship (International Association of Black Actuaries)
eligible_stage: Undergraduate or graduate student, min 3.0 GPA
citizenship: Open to Black students; U.S. enrollment typically required
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable — actuarial/finance focus does not match Cognitive Neuroscience.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Future opportunity once enrolled in college, if she pursues quantitative finance/actuarial coursework.
scholarships.notes: Only the top of the range clears the $5,000 floor.

scholarships.name: Sutton Trust US Programme (with Fulbright Commission)
scholarships.provider: The Sutton Trust / US-UK Fulbright Commission
scholarships.amount_display: Full mentoring + typically secures substantial need-based financial aid (average reported ~£138,500/$234,000 total over 4 years)
eligible_stage: Year 12 (UK) / 11th grade student at a UK STATE-FUNDED school
citizenship: Open to UK-resident students; separate from U.S. citizenship status
scholarships.residency_notes: Requires attendance at a UK state-funded (non-fee-paying) school AND historical Free School Meals eligibility (a low-income means-test) — verify whether Candidate B's school and family income meet this bar, as it is the main eligibility filter.
scholarships.nomination_notes: Selected through a competitive application, not a nomination, but requires the school to confirm state-funded/FSM status.
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable — UK-based program for UK students, and A is already enrolled in the U.S.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Directly eligible now as a Year 12 (11th grade) UK student — the single most relevant 'currently actionable' program on this list for her, IF her school is state-funded and she meets the income criteria. If she attends a fee-paying/independent UK school, she will not qualify — verify immediately.
scholarships.notes: Not a scholarship itself but a mentoring pipeline that leads directly to large need-based aid packages at top U.S. universities (Fulbright Commission-run).

scholarships.name: Benjamin A. Gilman International Scholarship
scholarships.amount_display: Up to $5,000 (plus Critical Need Language Award up to $8,000 additional)
eligible_stage: Currently-enrolled U.S. undergraduate, Pell-Grant eligible, planning study/internship abroad
scholarships.residency_notes: For U.S. college students going abroad, not for students already abroad applying to enter the U.S.
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Future opportunity — relevant only if A pursues a study-abroad term later in her Brown career and is Pell-eligible.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Not applicable.
scholarships.notes: Included for completeness on the 'study abroad' funding angle; not immediately actionable for either candidate.

scholarships.name: Foot Locker Scholar Athletes Program
scholarships.amount_display: $20,000 (paid $5,000/year over 4 years)
eligible_stage: High school senior, competitive athlete
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable unless she is a competitive varsity athlete — flagged for completeness only.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Not applicable unless she is a competitive varsity athlete — flagged for completeness only.
scholarships.notes: Included to show the athletics angle exists in the database, even though neither profile currently indicates varsity athletics.

scholarships.name: Point Foundation Flagship Scholarship
scholarships.amount_display: Varies, up to full need + mentorship, historically $5,000-$40,000/year
eligible_stage: High school senior or current undergraduate
scholarships.residency_notes: Restricted to LGBTQ+-identifying applicants — noted for completeness, not matched to either profile as described.
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable based on the profile shared.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Not applicable based on the profile shared.
scholarships.notes: Shown only to illustrate the breadth of the minority-scholarship landscape captured in this tool; remove if not needed.

scholarships.name: Psi Chi / Society for Neuroscience Undergraduate Research Awards
scholarships.provider: Psi Chi (International Honor Society in Psychology) / Society for Neuroscience
scholarships.amount_display: Up to $6,000 (research grant, not tuition scholarship)
eligible_stage: Currently-enrolled undergraduate conducting original research, typically sophomore+
citizenship: Open internationally, some awards U.S.-restricted — verify per award
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Future opportunity — not available freshman year, but directly relevant once A begins Cognitive Neuroscience research at Brown (typically sophomore year+). Worth bookmarking now.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Not applicable — enrolled-undergraduate research award.
scholarships.notes: A research grant rather than a tuition scholarship, but real cash funding tied exactly to A's intended major.

scholarships.name: Regeneron Science Talent Search (STS)
scholarships.amount_display: $25,000-$250,000 (top prize); all 40 finalists receive at least $25,000
eligible_stage: High school senior with an independent research project
citizenship: Open to U.S. and international students attending U.S.-recognized high schools, and select international schools
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable this cycle — this is a pre-matriculation senior-year competition; A has already been admitted to Brown.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Future opportunity if she pivots toward research-heavy STEM (currently profiled as business/psychology/finance) — flagged for completeness given the neuroscience-adjacent research angle in the family.
scholarships.notes: The single largest-value pre-college research award in the U.S.; requires a completed original research project.

scholarships.name: U.S. Bank Student Scholarship
scholarships.amount_display: Multiple awards; top awards up to $20,000, most-modules-completed track pays $5,000
eligible_stage: High school senior (17+) or current undergraduate
scholarships.residency_notes: No-essay, financial-literacy-module based; open to incoming and current undergrads.
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Directly eligible now — open to enrolled undergraduates, not just incoming seniors; low-effort application (complete financial literacy modules).
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Not applicable — U.S. residency required.
scholarships.notes: One of the few general awards genuinely open to an already-enrolled college freshman like Candidate A.

scholarships.name: Common Knowledge Scholarship Foundation Award
eligible_stage: High school senior or current undergraduate, depending on cycle
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Possible fit — verify current-cycle eligibility for enrolled freshmen vs. incoming seniors only.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Future opportunity — verify current-cycle rules senior year.
scholarships.notes: Smaller/lesser-known foundation; always double check the live eligibility page as these details shift.

scholarships.name: Elks National Foundation Legacy Award
scholarships.amount_display: $4,000-$12,500 total over 4 years (varies by rank)
eligible_stage: High school senior, child/grandchild of an active Elks member
scholarships.residency_notes: Requires a parent/grandparent to be an Elks member in good standing — unlikely to apply unless the family already has an Elks Lodge connection.
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable unless a family member is an Elks Lodge member.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Not applicable unless a family member is an Elks Lodge member.
scholarships.notes: Included for completeness; likely a non-match unless there is an existing Elks family connection.

scholarships.name: Dr. Soronnadi Nnaji Legacy Scholarship
scholarships.deadline: ~June annually (recent cycles closed early-mid June — confirm on Bold.org)
eligible_stage: High school senior OR current 2-year/4-year undergraduate — no class-year restriction
citizenship: Open regardless of citizenship status; first- or second-generation African immigrant
scholarships.residency_notes: Preference given to students active in African student associations at their school.
field_of_study: Any STEM major, incl. Cognitive Neuroscience
scholarships.minority_group: First- or second-generation African immigrant (directly matches Nigerian origin)
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Directly eligible now — one of the strongest matches on this list: Nigerian/African immigrant background, STEM major, and open to current undergraduates (not seniors-only). Apply this cycle.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Future opportunity once enrolled in college as an undergraduate (not open to pre-college students).
scholarships.notes: Named for Dr. Soronnadi Nnaji, established by his daughters in his honor; strongly prefers African student-association involvement — worth joining Brown's African Students Association.

scholarships.name: UNCF / Merck Undergraduate Science Research Scholarship
scholarships.provider: United Negro College Fund (UNCF) with Merck
scholarships.amount_display: Up to $25,000/year
scholarships.deadline: Typically opens November, closes mid-January — confirm on UNCF portal each cycle
eligible_stage: Currently-enrolled underrepresented-minority undergraduate in STEM
scholarships.residency_notes: Open beyond UNCF's HBCU member schools in past cycles, but confirm the current participating-school list before applying — this is the key eligibility risk for a Brown student.
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Strong potential match — verify Brown is on the current list of eligible institutions before applying; if so, this is a top-tier fit (minority + STEM + open to enrolled undergrads).
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Not applicable — for currently-enrolled undergraduates only.
scholarships.notes: Highly competitive (~15 awarded nationally per year).

scholarships.name: Carson Scholars Fund
scholarships.amount_display: $1,000 (below the $5,000 floor — included because it's genuinely actionable right now)
eligible_stage: Grades 4-11 — directly open to her THIS year as an 11th grader
citizenship: Must attend an accredited K-12 school in the United States
scholarships.residency_notes: Requires U.S.-based school attendance — verify whether her UK school (if American/international-curriculum) qualifies, since the program is written around U.S. K-12 schools.
scholarships.nomination_notes: REQUIRES nomination by an educator at her school; only one student per school per year can be nominated.
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable — grades 4-11 only, she has already graduated high school.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Potentially actionable THIS YEAR (11th grade) if her school qualifies as a U.S.-accredited K-12 school — worth asking her school directly given the UK-residency question. Good low-stakes practice with the nomination process even though below the $5,000 floor.
scholarships.notes: Below the requested $5,000 minimum; included because it is one of the only nomination-based awards she is grade-eligible for immediately.

scholarships.name: United States Senate Youth Program
scholarships.amount_display: $10,000 undergraduate scholarship + fully-funded Washington Week program
scholarships.deadline: Varies by state, typically applications open ~mid-August and close ~September-October
eligible_stage: High school junior or senior holding an elected/appointed student-leadership role
scholarships.residency_notes: Administered state-by-state through U.S. public/private high schools (plus DoDEA overseas schools) — confirm with her school whether it participates in a U.S. state's selection process, since most independent international schools are not part of this pipeline.
field_of_study: Any / Undeclared — encourages history/political science/business-adjacent interests
scholarships.nomination_notes: REQUIRES nomination by the high school principal; a principal may nominate up to 2 students from the same school.
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable — for currently-enrolled high school juniors/seniors, not college students.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Directly eligible now IF she holds (or can attain) a student-leadership role and her school can participate in a U.S. state's nomination pipeline — worth raising with her school counselor this fall given the UK-residency complication.
scholarships.notes: One of the few high-value ($10,000+) awards genuinely open to juniors right now, contingent on the school's ability to nominate through a U.S. state.

scholarships.name: Jackie Robinson Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.amount_display: Up to $35,000 over four years + four-year mentoring program
eligible_stage: High school senior
scholarships.residency_notes: Requires financial need documentation and plans to attend an accredited U.S. 4-year institution.
scholarships.minority_group: Open to all backgrounds; strong track record of supporting Black/African-descent scholars
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable — for incoming high school seniors, not enrolled college students.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Future opportunity — apply fall/winter of 12th grade if financial need applies.
scholarships.notes: Comes with a strong four-year mentoring and career-placement program beyond the cash award.

scholarships.name: Posse Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.amount_display: Full-tuition scholarship to a Posse partner college (value varies by school; excludes room/board)
scholarships.deadline: Nominations open spring/summer of junior year; interviews run through senior fall
eligible_stage: Nominated as early as second semester of 11th grade
citizenship: Not restricted to a specific minority group; open broadly
scholarships.residency_notes: Nomination must come through a Posse-registered U.S. high school or community-based organization in one of ~20 U.S. recruitment cities — confirm whether her UK school (or a U.S.-based college-access program she can join remotely) is a Posse partner, since this is the main barrier for a UK-based applicant.
scholarships.nomination_notes: REQUIRES nomination by a Posse-partner high school or community organization — self-nomination is not accepted.
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable — nomination process happens in high school, before college enrollment.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Timing lines up now (nominations start spring of 11th grade), but the U.S.-city partner-school requirement is a real obstacle given her UK residence — worth investigating whether a Posse-affiliated program accepts international/UK-based nominees.
scholarships.notes: Highly competitive (roughly 1 in 24 nominees selected in recent cycles).

scholarships.name: NSHSS + DECA Scholarship
scholarships.provider: National Society of High School Scholars (NSHSS) with DECA
scholarships.amount_display: Historically ~$2,000-$5,000 — confirm current-cycle amount
scholarships.deadline: Varies by cycle — check NSHSS scholarship calendar
eligible_stage: High school junior or senior, NSHSS member AND active DECA member
citizenship: Open to U.S. and international students
scholarships.residency_notes: Requires both NSHSS membership (educator-nomination based) and an active DECA chapter membership.
scholarships.nomination_notes: NSHSS membership requires an educator nomination; stack this with an active DECA membership.
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable — business/finance focus doesn't match Cognitive Neuroscience.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Directly relevant now — ask a teacher to submit her NSHSS educator nomination this year, and confirm whether her school has (or can start) a DECA chapter.
scholarships.notes: Open internationally, unlike several U.S.-only nomination programs on this list — worth prioritizing given her UK location.

scholarships.name: NSHSS Membership & Scholarship Network
scholarships.provider: National Society of High School Scholars (NSHSS)
scholarships.amount_display: Individual member scholarships range roughly $1,000-$10,000 depending on award
scholarships.deadline: Rolling — individual scholarships open/close throughout the year
eligible_stage: High-achieving high school student, 3.5+ GPA or equivalent test scores
scholarships.residency_notes: An educator must nominate the student for NSHSS membership; members then apply to subject-specific scholarships (business, STEM, leadership, entrepreneurship, etc.).
field_of_study: Any, depending on the specific award
scholarships.nomination_notes: Membership itself is nomination-based (an educator nominates the student); once a member, she applies directly to individual scholarships.
scholarships.candidate_a_fit: Not applicable — NSHSS targets high school students, not enrolled college undergraduates.
scholarships.candidate_b_fit: Directly actionable now — genuinely open internationally (a rarity among nomination programs), so this is one of the highest-priority 'ask a teacher to nominate me' actions for her this year.
scholarships.notes: Functions as a gateway (membership) into a wide internal scholarship pool rather than a single award — treat the NSHSS row as an entry point.
